item.title: CISA adds actively exploited Collabora Online document leak CVE-2026-10521 and Arista VeloCloud SD WAN flaws to KEV catalog
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity authorities have updated the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog under Binding Operational Directive 22-01, issuing emergency patch mandates for two actively weaponized enterprise software vulnerabilities. Unauthenticated remote adversaries exploit document rendering handlers and SD-WAN management portals to exfiltrate corporate files and execute arbitrary code across perimeter subnets.
The emergency additions feature Collabora Online unauthenticated document leakage vulnerability CVE-2026-10521 alongside remote command execution flaws impacting Arista VeloCloud SD-WAN edge appliances. Threat telemetry confirms adversaries actively weaponizing Collabora rendering endpoints embedded in Nextcloud and cloud storage servers to leak unencrypted document buffers and session tokens. Federal civilian executive branch agencies face a mandatory October 26 compliance deadline to apply official vendor security updates.
Subverting cloud document servers and SD-WAN perimeter routers destroys data confidentiality and network boundary controls. Because Collabora servers process sensitive enterprise files in memory and VeloCloud gateways manage corporate site-to-site traffic routing, unauthenticated exploitation permits threat actors to extract confidential records and pivot into core production subnets.
- Force immediate installation of official maintenance updates across all self-hosted Collabora Online document server instances. - Apply emergency security patches published for Arista VeloCloud SD-WAN edge routers and restrict WAN management access. - Restrict public internet visibility of Collabora rendering endpoints by placing document servers behind zero trust access proxies. - Inspect network perimeter logs for anomalous data exfiltration volumes or unverified administrative calls targeting SD-WAN gateways.
Enterprise cloud suite defense demands rapid patch execution and strict microsegmentation to ensure document collaboration infrastructure and SD-WAN perimeters remain protected against active wild exploitation. #CodeDefence #Collabora #Arista #VeloCloud #CISA #KEV #CloudSecurity #SDWAN #AppSec #PatchManagement

item.title: Global WAF telemetry tracks Black October automated scanning wave targeting PHP2Shell core vulnerabilities
item.description:
Cyber threat research writeups published today warn of unprecedented automated scanning volumes hitting global web application firewalls. Security analysts dubbed the ongoing campaign Black October as automated botnets attempt mass exploitation of memory allocation defects in core web runtimes.
The ongoing attack wave targets PHP core vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Unauthenticated remote adversaries transmit malformed multipart HTTP request headers designed to trigger uninitialized array hash table allocation bugs, executing remote system commands under the web server context before application logic processes incoming traffic. Security telemetry indicates threat groups utilizing automated script arrays to scan millions of IP addresses per hour, attempting to plant persistent web shells and cryptominers.
Subverting core web application engines exposes hosting infrastructure and backend database servers. Because PHP processes web traffic for enterprise web portals, digital storefronts, and cloud APIs, an unauthenticated core remote code execution flaw allows threat actors to establish covert footholds and exfiltrate database credentials.
- Upgrade production PHP web application runtimes immediately to fixed maintenance releases 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35. - Configure web application firewall WAF rules to inspect and strip malformed multipart POST requests on non-upload endpoints. - Inspect web server hosting directories for unauthorized shell scripts or newly modified executable files. - Monitor host process execution trees for anomalous command prompt or shell invocations originating from web worker daemons.
Web application runtime defense requires rapid dependency patch execution and strict edge request filtering to ensure central web hosting infrastructure remains protected against automated botnet exploitation. #CodeDefence #PHP #PHP2Shell #RCE #AppSec #WebSecurity #ZeroDay #PatchManagement #ThreatIntelligence #DevSecOps

item.title: CERT In issues mandatory security advisory governing autonomous AI agent deployments across enterprise networks
item.description:
National cybersecurity regulators have issued formal security guidance establishing mandatory risk controls for organizations deploying autonomous artificial intelligence agents. The advisory highlights emerging attack vectors where automated agent reasoning chains are manipulated to execute unauthorized system commands or exfiltrate corporate data.
The regulatory directive released by CERT-In outlines key security requirements for agent-based AI integrations. The framework flags risks associated with indirect prompt injection, goal hijacking, and unmonitored non-human identity API privileges. Mandated controls include enforcing least-privilege role-based access limits on AI agents, implementing mandatory human-in-the-loop checkpoints for high-stakes financial transactions or database modifications, and maintaining immutable audit logs of agent decision pathways.
Granting excessive system execution permissions to autonomous AI agents introduces severe software supply chain and data governance risks. When AI agents process untrusted external context or email bodies without input sanitization, malicious payloads can hijack agent reasoning loops, forcing agents to exfiltrate database records or execute unauthorized API calls.
- Enforce least-privilege scoping across non-human service principal tokens and API integration keys assigned to AI agents. - Implement human-in-the-loop authorization gates for autonomous AI agent actions involving database writes or financial transactions. - Deploy input sanitization layers to strip indirect prompt injection payloads from external web pages, emails, and document strings. - Maintain centralized, immutable logging of AI agent reasoning steps, API calls, and decision outputs for forensic auditing.
Artificial intelligence governance demands rigid permission boundaries and continuous decision auditing to ensure autonomous agent workflows remain protected against indirect prompt injection and goal hijacking exploitation. #CodeDefence #AISecurity #CERT_In #AIGovernance #PromptInjection #IdentitySecurity #APISecurity #DevSecOps #AppSec
